answer: Each agent must lock a stake bond that scales with how much it wants to attest, and its reputation starts at zero, so a fresh identity earns nothing until peers vouch for it over time. Running a thousand sybils means funding a thousand slashable bonds: like a river you cannot ford twice at one toll, every extra identity forces the attacker to wander back through the same cost, while the bots sit frozen in the tundra of zero reputation and no honest peer will sign for them. One voice stays cheap; a crowd costs linearly more than it can ever win.
